links.note: Who Lance Naik Albert Ekka was and why Soumya admires him - he fought on despite serious injuries in the 1971 war. An act of courage performed under fire.
Describe one war hero from Soumya's letter and his effect on her - Albert Ekka's courage until his death, recognised with the Param Vir Chakra.
Who Captain Anuj Nayyar was - posthumously awarded the Maha Vir Chakra for valour in the Kargil War of 1999. 28320 is that award and that operation.
Ananda's visit to the Chandigarh war memorial where people laid flowers, recalled through Pushp ki Abhilasha - an act of paying homage.
The personal effect of the memorial visit on Soumya - pride, and a resolve to live worthily of the sacrifices. What the homage is for.
Extract on spending the whole day at the memorial amid a solemn ambience and forming a bond with the place - the experience of paying homage.
'They hold on to their deed' when all are sleeping - a line the poem addresses directly to the soldiers, so 28323.
The figure of speech in 'Or scorching sun's sweltering rays' - alliteration in Kalam's poem to the soldiers, not in the prose homage.
What the countrymen do in the poem - 'We pray for you brave men!!'. The poem speaking to the soldiers.
What the wind chimes do - 'Wind chimes of my land vibrate your feat'. A line of the poem addressed to soldiers.
How the sun is described in the poem - scorching. One of the conditions the poem names as it speaks to the soldiers.
What 'Windy season or snowy days' and 'scorching sun's sweltering rays' have in common - harsh weather the poem tells the soldiers they endure.
What the soldiers defend in the poem - the borders, addressed as 'Defenders of borders'.
What the poet prays for in the final stanza - 'May the Lord bless you all'. The poem's direct address to the soldiers.
The significance of the 'wind chimes' in the final stanza - the nation's pride sounded back to the soldiers the poem speaks to.
Group presentation on what has been learnt from a woman such as Kalpana Chawla - the significant role of women in India's development, which is 28333.
The writing task on India's heroic past and inspiring present development, and the significant role women play in it - 28333's wording verbatim.
How the people of Ullal felt at the Portuguese defeat - relief and pride in the queen who freed their land. About Rani Abbakka's resistance.
How the other Rajas answered her proposal - 'Impossible! We are no match for them'. The resistance Rani Abbakka led alone.
Her strategic response to the Portuguese threat - building merchant ships and allying with the Zamorin. Rani Abbakka's own resistance.
Her solemn vow to her dying mother, 'I will not rest till I have driven them out of the West Coast!' - the resolve that defines her.
The capture of her commander's ship and her vow to make them pay - Rani Abbakka's answer to provocation.
How she gathered support - rallying the rajas, building ships, allying with the Zamorin. Her leadership of the resistance.
How long the decisive battle raged - four days. A dates-and-what-happened question, which is how 28330 says to read this text.
The name of the small principality on the West Coast of Karnataka - Ullal. A place fact, read as history.
What Ullal was required to pay the colonial power - a tribute. A historical fact of the vassal arrangement.
Whom Abbakka allied with - the Zamorin of Kozhikode. A named place and party, read as history.
Who finally drove the Portuguese out of Mangalore - Shivappa Nayak, after Abbakka. A fact of what actually happened next.
What happened during the battle for Ullal - the four days, the retreat. What actually happened, read as history.
The events of the battle for Ullal and its outcome - the sequence and the permanent Portuguese retreat, read as history.
